planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container-grown shrubs in spring in fertile, humus-rich, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in partial shade to full sun.

directions: Port Wine is the most widely sold purple-flowered selection of banana shrub, its blooms a deep, saturated wine-maroon rather than the species' creamy yellow with a thin maroon edge, carrying the same intensely sweet, banana-custard fragrance that makes a single flowering shrub perfume an entire garden. It forms the same dense, slow-growing, rounded evergreen frame as the species, flowering heaviest in spring with scattered rebloom into summer in milder zones. Site it in part shade with some relief from the harshest afternoon sun to keep the deep flower color from fading and the glossy foliage from bleaching, and avoid hard pruning since flower buds set on the previous season's wood. Established plants are tough and low-maintenance, tolerating brief drought and needing only an occasional light shaping to stay tidy.
sources: Trees and Shrubs Online (International Dendrology Society)
